one_star_reviews.text:
I used Blue Clean Services for both a deep clean and steam cleaning of a sofa bed, fabric chair and rug.

The steam cleaning was completed satisfactorily, but unfortunately I was very disappointed with the $412 deep clean. When I returned home, there was still visible hair and debris on the floors, dust on surfaces including the fridge, cobwebs remaining, window areas that had not been properly cleaned, and visible dirt remaining in the bathroom/toilet areas. These were all things I reasonably expected to be addressed as part of a deep clean.

I have used other cleaning companies in the past where they sent more cleaners and allowed enough time to properly complete a deep clean, rather than trying to compress the work into such a short period. Given the price and the scope of the service, I expected a much more thorough result.

I raised the issues with Blue Clean and provided photographic evidence. To their credit, they acknowledged that several areas included in the deep-cleaning scope had not been completed to the expected standard and offered to return to rectify the work. However, after the initial experience I had lost confidence in the service and did not want the additional inconvenience of another visit, particularly with a six-month-old baby at home.

They ultimately offered an $88 refund. While I appreciated that some refund was offered, I did not feel this adequately reflected the extent of the issues with a $412 deep-cleaning service.

In hindsight, I wish I had paid more attention to some of the poorer reviews before booking, as parts of my experience were consistent with the concerns raised by other customers.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Blue Clean Services for a deep clean.
Price assessment
Overpriced

one_star_reviews.text:
An absolutely woeful experience dealing with Flooring Xtra across the Eltham branch, Nunawading branch and even their head office. Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend spending a little more and going elsewhere for better service, workmanship and, most importantly, some form of after-sales support.

My first mistake was contacting the Nunawading store for a quote. I sent through the floor plan as requested and followed up twice. No response whatsoever.

Against my better judgement, I then tried the Eltham store. The store opened around 10 minutes late and, from the outset, there seemed to be very little interest in actually earning the business.

I dealt with Warwick, who came out, measured the job and took the deposit. Interestingly, once the deposit had been paid, the level of interest seemed to disappear very quickly.

Installation day was where things really went downhill. Once the job was supposedly “completed”, the installer began making excuses for why the joins could not be finished neatly, blaming the material. There were also areas where the carpet had bunched up and other sections that, in my view, were simply poorly installed.

The old saying about a poor tradesman blaming his tools immediately came to mind. Perhaps if as much time had been spent concentrating on the installation as was spent taking cigarette breaks in the car, the finished product may have at least been somewhere near acceptable.

I emailed Warwick outlining the issues and was told he would speak with the installers and get back to me.

He didn’t.

I then sent another four emails.

Radio silence.

Eventually, I contacted Flooring Xtra head office and explained both the workmanship issues and the complete lack of communication from the Eltham store. Unsurprisingly, I have received absolutely no response from head office either.

Then, almost magically, the Eltham store manager contacted me the following day saying he had been away from work, had just returned, and would be in touch to arrange rectification.

That also went nowhere.

Another follow-up email has since been sent and, once again, there has been no communication.

The recurring theme here is very simple: they appear extremely efficient when it comes to taking your money, but once they have been paid, good luck getting anybody to respond when there is a problem.

Poor workmanship can happen. What separates a reputable business from a poor one is how they deal with the problem afterwards. In my case, the after-sales service has been virtually nonexistent.

My advice would be to avoid the chain altogether and use a reputable independent flooring company that actually values its customers after the invoice has been paid.

An expensive lesson learned.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am very disappointed with this experience and have serious concerns about the way the additional works were quoted and justified.

I called Carlingford Plumbing regarding a blocked sink, but the plumber who attended was from Fixed Today Plumbing Beecroft.

The plumber attended and found that the issue was actually a tripped GPO/outlet for the pump, which was not a plumbing issue. The plumber then said they had contacted their electrician contacts and advised that the existing GPO needed to be replaced, a separate GPO needed to be installed for the pump because the pump was supposedly too powerful to share the existing GPO with the microwave, and a new RCBO also needed to be installed.

What concerned me most was the way the electrical works were assessed and justified.

When the electrician arrived, their initial response was simply to switch/reset the existing GPO. They then repeatedly asked the plumber what had been quoted and what work they were supposed to carry out. As a customer, I would expect a licensed electrician to independently assess the electrical issue and provide their own professional opinion, rather than relying on the plumber to tell them what had been quoted.

I questioned the need for the new GPO several times before the work was carried out. However, after the electrician was told that installing a new GPO was part of the quotation, they then firmly maintained that it was required, otherwise the existing GPO would supposedly trip again.

The same thing happened with the RCBO. After the new GPO was installed, the electrician consulted the plumber again about whether a new RCBO was actually required. The plumber said it was not. The electricians were then preparing to finish the job. When I pointed out that a new RCBO was also included in the quotation, they suddenly decided that the RCBO was required after all.

This was extremely concerning to me. I had questioned the necessity of these works before they were undertaken, yet the justification appeared to change depending on what had been included in the quotation. I would expect the licensed electrician to independently determine what electrical work was actually required based on the electrical installation and the relevant requirements, rather than confirming that work was necessary simply because it had already been quoted.

I am also disappointed that, despite raising these concerns before the work was undertaken, I was not given a clear and consistent technical explanation for why the additional works were necessary.

Overall, I found the quoting process unclear, the communication between the plumber and electrician concerning, and the justification for the electrical works inconsistent. Based on my experience, I would not use this service again or recommend it to others.

Contacted Stegbar to get a quote regarding a new shower screen. Regency Shower Screens and Wardrobes (affiliated with Stegbar I assume) contacted me and organised quote. I was required to pay in full upfront when accepting quote. Shower screen installed. A few days after install I noticed damage to my cavity door. The shower screen bracket had been secured to the wall which contained a cavity door. Not an issue if the correct size screw is used. In this case it wasn’t and the screws had gone through the wall into the cavity. The sliding cavity door was now hitting the screws and had scratched and damaged the door.

I contacted Regency and after some initial suggestion about this being a warranty claim (it wasn’t, it was incorrect installation) it was agreed that someone would come and replace the fixing. That took about 5 days. It took another 3 weeks of back and forth for some sort of resolution regarding fixing the door itself. I received a call saying someone would come, remove the door and fix it off site. Apparently this is easier for them. The process of fixing would take 5 days I was told.

We only have one bathroom so not having a bathroom door for 5 days with two teenagers is unacceptable considering this was an issue created by the installer. I gave up trying to get Stegbar and Regency to take the matter seriously and fix it promptly. I repaired it myself at my own cost and time.

Yes I could have fixed it myself all along but as a matter of principle I genuinely thought the company who damaged my door due to poor installation should take the matter seriously and resolve the issue promptly. After a month of chasing them I gave up. Like 99% of the tradies out there, once they have your money you go to the bottom of priority list.

Post install customer service poor. I won’t bother using this company again.

one_star_reviews.text:
🚨⚠️DISEASE CARRYING  FISH⚠️🚨

Bought a gold fish from here to add to an established 100 litre tank with 2 fantails and 4 tetras... It was infected with white spot/ich.

One week later everything in our 100 litre tank of goldfish that are nearly a decade old are all dead.  Absolutely gutted. These fish have lived through moving house twice and moving states once, only to be posioned by Petbarn.

There is obviously no quarantine protocol at petbarn for fish to ensure they are not spreading diseases. Went back to discuss only to see everything but 3 fish in their tanks are also dead. The 3 that are left were in the process of dying- 2 were eating the body of the third.

The young girl was nice enough,, apologetic, refunded the 11 bucks,and admitted they didnt know why their fish were all dying ( clearly have no knowledge of ich disease) - but now our entire tank has been decimated thanks to their negligence.

In over a decade of having fish  (purchased from a reputable aquarium) I have never witnessed anything so upsetting. White spot/ich will suffocate your fish slowly, horrific to watch and by the time they have symptoms its too late. Their little bodies will contort and twist in pain as they are unable to breathe slowly suffocating to death.

🚨DO NOT BUY ANY KIND OF AQUATIC LIFE FROM HERE UNLESS PREPARED TO LOSE ALL OF YOUR FISH🚨

Pictured is our beautiful female Nadja, our 6 year old 15cm long fantail in an empty tank. All the red around her gills is from oxygen starvation.
Tinge to the water is from ich x treatment which was was administered as soon as the small tetras started  showing symptoms. First to die was the new baby fish after 5 days in the tank. Tetras died within 24 hrs after. The large gold fish struggled for another 24 hours and died.

Absolutely disgusted 🤮🤬

Edit: Regarding your reply, this is adding insult to injury. Not only have I had already spoken with the assistant store manager where despite her poor service, it was confirmed the shipment of fish was recieved only the day prior to sale and there is no company protocol, policy or best practice exercised in quarantining of any sort. They are simply placed on display to be sold. I have also already reported this directly to your head office and filed a formal complaint.

If you want to sell live animals you have a responsibility to customers to advise them by way of a sign that the fish you sell present a risk of disease. The lack of accountability is bewildering as is your response.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this university has been extremely disappointing, particularly when it comes to student support, administration and placement coordination. Unfortunately, this is not just my experience. Many other students have experienced the same issues and expressed similar frustrations.

The level of support from the university has been extremely poor. There appears to be very little communication, accountability or genuine concern for students. Important tasks and arrangements are repeatedly left until the last minute, creating unnecessary stress and making it difficult for students to meet their requirements and deadlines.

The organisation of placements has been particularly frustrating. Placements should be arranged weeks, if not months, in advance, especially when students are required to complete more than 100 hours of training from home before commencing their placement. Instead, students can be left waiting for information and then told only days before their placement where they are expected to go. This does not provide enough time to properly organise, prepare or complete the required training.

What makes this even more frustrating is that these problems appear to be ongoing and are affecting multiple students, not just one individual. There seems to be a recurring pattern of poor planning, last-minute communication and a lack of accountability from those responsible for coordinating and supporting students.

The quality of administration, coordination and facilitation has been extremely disappointing. Students should not have to constantly chase staff for information, repeatedly ask for assistance or worry about whether essential requirements will be organised in time. When issues arise, there often seems to be little ownership, with students left feeling as though they have to solve problems that were created by poor university processes.

Trying to organise placement through the university has been unnecessarily stressful and frustrating for many students. Students deserve better communication, organisation and support, particularly when placements and mandatory training can have a direct impact on their ability to progress through their course.

If I had the opportunity to make the decision again, I would seriously consider attending a different university. Based on both my experience and the experiences I have heard from other students, I would strongly encourage prospective students to carefully research the level of support, administration and placement coordination provided before enrolling.

BEWARE — Horrible builder.

My wife and I recently purchased a high-end custom home built by these guys. The house is plastered all over the Fairmont Homes website and was actually built for the owner, Daniel Logue, who resided in it for five years.

To our surprise, just three days after moving in, we discovered a major leak coming from the upstairs bathroom. We had several different tradespeople come out, and they all pointed out that the incorrect falls in the shower floor have caused premature failure of the waterproofing.

Attached to this review are photos of the shower floor gradient, which clearly show how non-compliant the falls are. In fact, they are not just insufficient — on one side, the floor falls in the wrong direction, away from the drain.

As you would expect from a typical builder, they are denying liability and using the "out of warranty" card regarding the matter. Houses three times as old and a third of the cost haven't had these types of defects. It's embarrassing that they call themselves a custom home builder.

I hope this review saves many other hard-working Australians from spending their hard-earned money with Fairmont Homes, only to find themselves in this type of situation.

All we wanted was a shower that works as it should. Even after Daniel Logue came out and inspected the situation, he has avoided commenting on the non-compliant falls.

And it doesn't end there. We then inspected the other two bathrooms, only to find that they are just as bad. Luckily, they are on the ground level.

If I could leave them 0 stars, I would.

one_star_reviews.text:
Egregious administrative negligence, flawed desk audits, and zero accountability

As an experienced, professional insulation contractor operating Integrity Insulation, I have invested hundreds of hours, thousands of dollars in specialized equipment and tools, and absolute dedication to meeting rigorous industry regulations. Unfortunately, my experience with the Energy Efficiency Council’s (EEC) Certified Insulation Installer program has been a masterclass in administrative incompetence and procedural unfairness.

My application was subjected to a rushed, negligent desk-audit process. Despite completing nearly 99% of tasks, producing meticulous geotagged video and photo evidence for all work, and updating my coursework over more than 100 intensive hours, the assessment panel failed my application on major safety grounds specifically targeting LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) and Working at Heights. Furthermore, the panel falsely claimed my Certificate of Compliance for Electrical Work (CCEW) was missing, completely ignoring the fact that I had successfully uploaded it through their portal and even sent it separately via email.

When I sought to rectify minor documentation or clarify system glitches, I was denied basic natural justice or a reasonable window to respond. Instead, they rushed a formal failure, forcing me into a costly formal appeal process.

On 1 October 2026, the EEC’s independent Ombudsperson formally reviewed the matter and completely overturned and dismissed the panel's findings, vindicating my technical compliance and confirming that the CCEW and safety measures were entirely valid.

Despite their own Ombudsperson proving their technical panel was completely in the wrong, the EEC refused to refund my application and appeal fees totaling $1,885. To add insult to injury, Karla Paeglis and the management team issued a flat refusal, shut down all communication, and declared that I must pay standard fees and start entirely from scratch over systemic portal glitches and staff negligence.

For an organization tasked with upholding professional standards in the energy efficiency sector, treating legitimate trade contractors this way causing severe commercial harm, financial loss, and emotional distress is completely unacceptable. Industry professionals deserve a transparent, fair, and competent certification body, which the EEC has failed to deliver.

I refused to make another trip because it's 15km away from my home and said I would wait at the store. He eventually called the manager and agreed to replace the grinder. However, he only swapped the grinder and still didn't provide the original box.

This is one of the Transition Care Program (TCP) sites that Monash Health (Kingston Centre) uses as a dumping ground for elderly patients that they cannot safely discharge home.

During my mother's stay at Regis Dandenong North, from February 2026 to May 2026, there were multiple billing issues that should have been resolved before she was transferred to the Dandenong North site.

It came across as though Monash Health and Regis were not working well together and my family was bounced around from person to person, with no one really taking any accountability.

I feel that my mother experienced a lot of pain and her dignity was compromised because she was forced to do things that she clearly did not want to do under the guise of ticking boxes for her TCP program.

Staff were stern and saying the right things but it didn't come across warm and friendly at all.

Services that were listed in the brochures and website, such as hairdressing, were not offered, resulting in my father having to cut my mother's hair at her bedside.

I feel deeply concerned after reading other reviews for this site around the same time period, which motivates me to flag these concerns with the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission.

If you are faced with a TCP placement at this site, I highly recommend pushing back for the sake of your loved one.

I had a very disappointing experience with Dr Deepika. I was referred to a gynaecologist because I have PCOS symptoms and a polyp, and I went into the appointment hoping to finally have someone properly listen to my concerns. Unfortunately, I left feeling completely dismissed and unheard.

I have very irregular bleeding, severe ongoing acne, extremely oily skin, excess hair growth and, more recently, significant weight gain. I tried to explain that I exercise regularly and eat well, and that the changes in my weight have been genuinely affecting my wellbeing and confidence. Instead of feeling listened to, I felt like my concerns were minimised. I was told that my acne “wasn’t that bad” and that lots of younger girls have body-image issues. I was also told, in relation to my weight concerns, that I shouldn’t want to be “anorexic” or “like a stick.” I found these comments extremely insensitive and completely inappropriate, especially when I was trying to discuss genuine changes to my body and symptoms associated with PCOS.

I also felt that I was repeatedly talked over rather than being given the opportunity to properly explain what I was experiencing.

I was prescribed a birth control pill, despite my main concerns being my PCOS symptoms and the polyp I had been referred for. Unfortunately, since taking it, my skin has become significantly oilier and my acne has worsened, and I have not experienced the improvement I was hoping for. My GP was also surprised by the choice of medication given how problematic my acne already was.

I was also advised to leave my polyp in rather than have it removed, which I personally found concerning and was not expecting given that this was one of the reasons I had been referred to a gynaecologist in the first place.

I spent almost $300 on this appointment and walked away feeling worse about myself, my health and my appearance. I expected to be listened to, taken seriously and given appropriate advice regarding my symptoms, but instead I felt talked down to and dismissed.

I will not be returning to this doctor and, based on my experience, I would not personally recommend her. I really hope that other patients, particularly young women dealing with PCOS and body changes, are treated with more understanding and respect.

one_star_reviews.text:
Poor service, Loss of brain cells & confusing fuel payment process.

I stopped at 7-Eleven Springvale South at around 10:15pm on 27/09/2026 after finishing a long shift, simply wanting to quickly fill up before work the next day.

I waited at the pump for around 10 minutes, despite the employee watching me from inside, because the fuel had not been activated. I eventually went inside to ask why, and was told I had to pay before filling up. I was happy to prepay $40, but explained that I wanted to use Fuel Lock and asked for the discounted price to be applied before paying.

The employee insisted that I had to pay the full $40 first, fill up my car, and then return inside for a refund. I explained that I had used Fuel Lock before and had never had to do this, but he insisted that this was always how it worked.

After filling up, I had to walk back inside again to receive my refund, which was given to me in a large amount of silver coins. This entire process took around 20 minutes and was unnecessarily inconvenient.

What made even less sense was the employee’s explanation that customers have to prepay to prevent people from driving off without paying. If the pump does not automatically stop at the prepaid amount, a customer could theoretically prepay $10, fill their entire tank, and drive off anyway. Therefore, the reasoning given to me did not seem to actually prevent the issue he was describing.

On top of this, there were several people outside the store who were making me feel uncomfortable, meaning I had to walk past them multiple times throughout this process.

I also filled up earlier that morning and did not have this issue, so the explanation that this is “always” how the process works was particularly frustrating.

Overall, this was a very unnecessarily difficult experience for something that should have been a quick fuel stop. Staff need to be properly trained on the Fuel Lock process and provide customers with clear and accurate information.

In the end I lost brain cells, walked past three junkies multiple times feeling uncomfortable , wasted 20minutes of my life and ended up with large amounts of silver coins. Go elsewhere to another station.

I had a very disappointing experience at Bunnings Bayswater. I arrived around 40 minutes before closing and needed help finding three building materials for a DIY project. I had the names and specifications, but I’m not experienced with timber and plywood and simply needed some basic guidance.
I approached several staff members, but was mostly given aisle numbers rather than actual assistance. Some areas were already closed or unattended, and several staff appeared to be talking among themselves while we were clearly struggling to find what we needed.
The staff member responsible for the timber area was on a break, and when I approached him I was again directed to an aisle. I explained that the area appeared closed and was told to find someone there.
Eventually, I stopped a staff member operating a forklift. I do want to acknowledge that he genuinely tried to help us, helped locate the timber and was willing to assist with the cuts. He even had to ask another colleague twice before we received further assistance.
When we later went to pay, it wasn’t clear which checkout area was still open and there was little guidance despite staff seeing us heading towards a closed area.
When I expressed my frustration at the front, the response was essentially, “What do you expect? We’re about to close.”
I’m not a tradie — just a regular customer trying to complete a DIY project. If the store is open until 9 pm, I think customers arriving 40 minutes before closing should still be able to expect reasonable assistance. I appreciated the forklift staff member who did make an effort, but overall the experience was very disappointing.

The reception staff were very friendly, helpful, and welcoming. However, I felt that the waiting time was quite long. My appointment was scheduled for 11:54 am, but I was not seen until approximately 25 minutes later.

I was initially informed that the consultation fee would be $90 AUD, which I acknowledged and understood. During the consultation, the GP advised me that everything was fine. I was also informed that I had exceeded the standard consultation time of 15 minutes by approximately 3 minutes, making the consultation 18 minutes in total.

However, I was charged $170 for the visit. While I understand that additional fees may apply when the consultation exceeds the allocated time, I was disappointed by the significant increase in the fee for only an additional three minutes.

I would have appreciated being informed of the final cost before making the payment at reception, particularly as I was originally advised that the fee would be $90.

I understand that delays can happen, but I feel that the waiting time, which was approximately 25 minutes beyond my scheduled appointment time, should also have been taken into consideration. I find it difficult to understand why an additional three minutes of consultation resulted in such a substantial increase in the fee, especially when part of the delay was on the clinic’s side.

I hope you can review this matter and consider whether the additional charge was reasonable under the circumstances. I would also appreciate clearer communication regarding consultation fees and any additional charges before payment is taken.

If you are looking at the SA Government's Affordable Homes program and get assigned Rivergum Homes, look elsewhere.

We moved into our "turnkey" property in March and logged all maintenance items within the required 3-month window.
Six months later, major defects remain completely unresolved.
Whenever I request updates, I am continually met with administrative delays and excuses, including:
Claims that they are still awaiting contractor quotes.
Staff members being away on sick leave.
Promises that our issues will be "brought up at the next internal meeting" with no subsequent follow-through.
Told that trades have been allocated (yet we never hear from any of them).

Due to this prolonged lack of action, we obtained independent assessments from qualified, licensed trade professionals. The total estimated cost to rectify Rivergum’s outstanding defects is $25,000.
Disappointing performance from a state-preferred builder.
WE CAN IN NO WAY RECOMMEND RIVERGUM HOMES

Windows were ordered for our property.  They arrived with glazing missing (which is common practice aparantly due to weight issues in transporting them and the glazing is supposed to follow). The windows/frames were also delivered with multiple manufacturing issues.  Our builder lodged these issues with Stegbar Taren Point the day he installed them, a week after delivery (14/9).  The Taren Point store has done nothing to escalate the issues being logged with customer service and have the faults repaired.  Not getting answers from Taren Point, our builder then logged the issues directly with customer service the following week. I am now involved to help escalate the issue.  We have both been told, glazing takes up to 3 weeks from the time of logging the issue.  Service calls for repair take up to 5 weeks to have someone come out.  This is after my builder has made around 6 phone calls.  I have now called twice.
Stegbar seem completely relaxed about making people wait after they delivered a substandard product.  I have hired a scaffold, I have plasterers, builder and painters waiting to complete work until the issue is solved.  A manager was supposed to call me yesterday, no call.  I followed up today, she's away again.  DON'T EVER ORDER ANYTHING FROM STEGBAR!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

one_star_reviews.text:
This is NOT a family clinic

I cannot recommend Surrey Street Family Clinic. When our family was distressed and increasingly unwell, Dr Sam handled the situation rigidly and unhelpfully. When I explicitly explained that I was too unwell to attend the clinic and asked where I should seek care instead, I was refused an answer. Later that night, I was hospitalised as my illness progressively worsened.

For a practice that calls itself a Family Clinic, our experience involved lost testing, bungled communication and absolutely no family awareness in the treatment of an illness affecting our entire household.

Our whole family became extremely unwell with the same gastro illness, beginning with one of our children. We repeatedly followed up his test results because we were relying on them to understand what was spreading through our household. On three occasions, we were told that all tests were clear and no illness had been detected.

We eventually discovered that additional testing ordered by Dr Sam had not been accounted for and a specimen had been lost. While the lost specimen may have been the pathology provider’s error, the communication around it clearly failed. Dr Sam himself appeared unaware that he had ordered testing beyond the viral tests until we raised it.

By the time we finally spoke with Dr Sam himself, five days after the original testing, my other son was very sick and I was extremely unwell. We were trying to navigate a healthcare problem after the diagnostic plan we had relied upon had fallen apart.

Dr Sam repeatedly returned to the fact that the phone call was only about our child’s test results and refused to discuss a family treatment plan unless we attended the clinic in person the following day. I explained that I was too unwell to physically get there and requested telehealth. This was refused.

I then explicitly asked where I should seek care instead. Should I go to hospital, urgent care or call Nurse On Call? Asking where to seek care was not an unreasonable request. Dr Sam became defensive and chose not to answer the question and instead ended the conversation.

That night, the illness progressed further, my vital signs became unstable and I was hospitalised. I was treated with antibiotics due to concern about sepsis.

Following up a missing result does not compensate for the failure to help a deteriorating patient understand where to seek care. For a private practice calling itself a Family Clinic, there was remarkably little family care when we actually needed it. I would not recommend this clinic to other families.

*The receptionists are very nice

The reception staff were friendly and welcoming. Unfortunately, my experience with Dr Chen was disappointing.

The consultation felt like a rushed 10-minute GP appointment, with very little explanation or context regarding what was actually happening with my varicose veins or the treatment options available.

I was essentially given two options: go to the hospital for treatment or proceed with FibroVein injections. When Dr Chen asked if I had any questions, I raised a couple of concerns, only to be told, “You seem like you have a lot of questions. Here’s a form, read this.”

I found this response dismissive and unprofessional. When seeking medical advice, I expect to be given the time to understand my condition, the risks and benefits of the proposed treatments, and whether the recommended approach is likely to address the underlying problem.

After seeking a second opinion, I have further concerns about the original advice I received, particularly whether the proposed treatment would effectively address the underlying venous issue or simply provide a temporary or inadequate solution.

While the reception staff were excellent, the consultation itself left me feeling uninformed and frustrated. I believe patients deserve a thorough assessment, clear explanations and the opportunity to ask reasonable questions before making decisions about their treatment.

I definitely wouldn’t come back here

I was served by a staff member named Victoria. When I explained that I had an appointment booked for 11:00 am, she immediately told me that they do not do appointments. I clearly explained to her that I had come to the store yesterday and that the staff had booked me in for today. She was not willing to listen to what I was trying to explain.

I tried explaining this to her a second and then a third time because I initially thought perhaps she was unaware that appointments could be made for warranty claims. Instead of listening, she appeared impatient and dismissive. Eventually, I showed her the email confirmation proving that I had been booked for 11:00 am.

Only after seeing the confirmation did she speak to her manager. Her manager confirmed that yes, they do accept appointments. What disappointed me even more was that there was no apology or acknowledgement that I had been given incorrect information. Instead, the response was simply along the lines of, “We are doing it now.” I found this extremely rude and unprofessional.

I also felt uncomfortable with the way I was treated during the interaction. I felt that my English and accent were being judged, and I felt that she was laughing or reacting negatively while I was trying to communicate. As an Indian customer, this interaction left me feeling that I was being treated differently because of my background and the way I speak English. I cannot say what her intention was, but that is how the interaction made me feel.

I understand that staff can be busy and that warranty claims may have procedures to follow. However, customers should still be listened to and treated with patience, courtesy and respect.

I went to the store simply to make a genuine battery warranty claim and expected basic customer service. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing. I hope the store management reviews what happened and provides appropriate customer-service training to ensure other customers do not have a similar experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely frustrating Click & Collect experience at Lincraft Northcote.

I ordered and fully paid for 2 Mayfair & Bond Faux Leather Dining Chair Covers online for Click & Collect. On the morning of collection, Sophia emailed me saying they only had one available and asked whether I wanted a partial or full refund. What made an already disappointing situation worse was finishing that message with a 😁 smiling/laughing emoji. Considering they were giving me last-minute bad news about an order I had already paid for and arranged to collect, I found that very inappropriate and dismissive. I have attached the email screenshot so people can judge it for themselves.
Unfortunately, the experience became even worse when I arrived to collect the remaining cover. Staff could not find my item for more than 15 minutes. Sophia was then called to the counter and I was told there was an issue updating the bill/order. Despite the order already being fully paid, I was asked to make another payment while they sorted out their system. I refused to pay twice for an item I had already purchased.
Instead of simply resolving their internal system issue, I was kept waiting while there were arguments about what their system supposedly required and several phone calls were made. Altogether, what should have been a straightforward Click & Collect took around half an hour or more.
To top it off, the refund for the second cover that they could not supply was not processed there and then. I was told it would take another few days to process.
This has caused completely unnecessary inconvenience. I had already spent time and petrol travelling there for Click & Collect, and because they could not fulfil the order properly I now have to spend more time and petrol travelling elsewhere, potentially around two hours of additional driving, to get what I originally needed. Had I been told this properly earlier, I could simply have chosen delivery or bought elsewhere.
Stock shortages can happen. That is understandable. What is not acceptable is the way the situation was communicated and then handled in-store: the inappropriate emoji in the bad-news email, difficulty locating a supposedly ready Click & Collect item, asking a customer to pay again for an already-paid order, a lengthy delay while their system was sorted out, and then no immediate refund for the item they could not supply.
A very disappointing experience, particularly because much of the inconvenience could have been avoided with better communication and customer service.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with the way Keilor Basketball Association appears to manage some of its teams, particularly from Division 2 and above.

From my experience, there seems to be far too much emphasis on generating revenue, with not enough consideration given to the development, wellbeing and overall experience of the players and coaches. These are young athletes who deserve to be treated as more than just a source of income for the club.

Another major concern is the way some teams are coached. In many cases, parents are asked to coach their child’s team. While I appreciate the commitment of parents who volunteer their time, there can be an obvious conflict of interest when a coach’s own child is involved. It can create situations where game time and team selection are influenced by personal interests rather than what is best for the team as a whole.

A representative basketball program should have coaches who are focused on developing all players, making objective decisions and putting the team’s performance and development first. Players should earn their opportunities based on effort, ability, attitude and development — not simply because their parent is coaching the team.

I believe Keilor Basketball has an opportunity to do much better in this area. The club should be focused on developing young players, supporting its coaches and creating genuinely competitive and well-managed teams, rather than giving the impression that financial considerations come first.

The kids deserve better, and I hope the association takes this feedback seriously and looks at how its representative program is being managed.

I would not recommend Dr Tal for endometriosis or fertility issues.

I saw him after a year and a half of trying to conceive and almost a year of recurring endometriosis pain post-surgery. I explained that we had already attended an IVF clinic, decided IVF wasn't for us, and had now made the decision to stop trying altogether. Despite making this clear, IVF continued to be brought back into the conversation, including being told that if we wanted a child, it would be our only option.

My reason for seeing a specialist was to manage my endometriosis and recurrent pain now that we were no longer trying to conceive. I specifically wanted to discuss returning to the contraceptive pill and explained what was most important to me when choosing one.
There was no discussion about the different options, potential side effects or what might best suit my priorities. A pill was simply prescribed. After the appointment, I discovered the medication chosen was actually one I would have wanted to avoid based on the very concern I had raised.

I had sought specialist advice to make an informed choice about managing my condition, but instead felt the decision had been made for me rather than with me.
I also raised concerns about passing a clot approximately the size of my hand and a drastic shortening of my cycle. When I asked what could be causing these changes, I was simply told, “I don't know.” I understand medicine doesn't always provide definitive answers, but after paying $390 to see a specialist in this field, I reasonably expected some discussion of possible causes, whether further investigation was warranted, or at least some clinical guidance.
I also noticed Dr Tal looking at his watch several times and felt I was only in the consultation for around 15 minutes. Towards the end, I was told that he wasn't sure why I was there and that he hoped he had been clear.
I wanted specialist guidance on managing my endometriosis going forward.

I'm very easy-going with medical appointments and have never had an issue with any GP I've seen. I didn't expect a definitive explanation for everything. I did, however, expect expertise, meaningful discussion of my symptoms, respect for the decisions I had already made regarding fertility, and to be included in decisions about my treatment.

The negative reviews about Dr Anthony Milch are unfortunately very relatable. In my experience, his bedside manner was extremely poor, and I found his communication condescending and his attitude difficult to deal with.

His fees are also extremely high, particularly for someone who requires ongoing psychiatric care. What concerned me most, however, was the lack of continuity and attentiveness to my treatment. At almost every appointment, it felt as though he was unfamiliar with the medications I had been taking long-term, despite these being medications he was responsible for managing and renewing.

On multiple occasions, I felt scolded or spoken down to rather than listened to. Eventually, I became so uncomfortable seeing him alone that I felt I needed someone else present at my appointments.

Dr Milch took me on as a patient after my previous psychiatrist retired, leaving me without ongoing psychiatric care. Unfortunately, throughout my time with him, I often felt like a burden rather than a patient whose care mattered. It felt as though I was being managed because the practice needed to ensure I wasn’t left without psychiatric care, rather than because there was any genuine interest in my wellbeing.

The final incident was particularly frustrating. Dr Milch went on holiday and my appointment was subsequently moved, leaving me without enough medication to get me through to the rescheduled appointment. I was left having to chase up scripts and organise additional appointments myself to try to resolve the situation.

After I asked about seeing another psychiatrist at the practice following this experience, I was subsequently dismissed from the practice indefinitely.

For someone working in mental health, I found the overall experience incredibly disappointing. Patients seeking psychiatric care are already in a vulnerable position, and I believe they deserve to feel listened to, respected and properly supported. Unfortunately, that was not my experience with Dr Milch.

Very disappointing experience at Domino’s Forest Lake

We ordered two pizzas tonight,  a BBQ Chicken & Bacon pizza and a Prawn pizza.

The BBQ Chicken & Bacon pizza was extremely spicy. I’m not sure whether extra spices had been added or whether the wrong chicken was used, but it was definitely not what we expected or had eaten before.

The Prawn pizza was also poorly made, with several slices that didn’t even have prawns on them. When you order a prawn pizza, you’d reasonably expect prawns to be spread across the pizza.

Unfortunately, the biggest disappointment was actually the customer service when I called the store to raise the issue.

The lady who answered put me through to the manager. When he answered, he didn’t introduce himself or even greet me. He immediately responded in a very blunt and rude manner, basically telling me that this was the chicken they had been using for the past five years.

I explained that regardless of how long they had been using it, the chicken was extremely spicy, and I was simply calling to let them know there was an issue with the pizza.

His attitude throughout the conversation was extremely rude and unprofessional. I actually had to point out to him that he was being rude and ask for his name, to which he simply replied that he was the manager. Rather than trying to resolve the issue or even acknowledge my concern, he basically told me there was nothing he could do and ended the call.

I wasn’t calling to have an argument. I was giving the store the opportunity to address a genuine problem with our order.

Food can sometimes go wrong that happens. But the way a customer is treated when they raise a legitimate concern says a lot about a business.

Unfortunately, nothing was resolved, the pizzas were disappointing, and the manager’s attitude was even worse.

Very poor experience with Domino’s Forest Lake. I won’t be rushing back

one_star_reviews.text: Shocking Workmanship, Extensive Damages, and Zero AccountabilityDo not trust Midcoast 4WD Centre (VDL Group) with your vehicle. I took my Nissan Navara NP300 to this shop for an accessory and suspension fitment, and they returned it to me in a completely unroadworthy, unsafe condition, with multiple independent vehicle systems severely damaged.1. Gross Mechanical Incompetence & Sagging Suspension (Front & Rear)My vehicle has successfully run a functional 2-inch lift and wide tyre package for over 7 years with zero clearance issues. Midcoast completely failed to weigh my vehicle or correctly calculate its permanent accessory load (canopy, fridge, solar panel, roof racks, and a heavy long-range fuel tank).Their own handwritten pre-inspection sheet records that my rear end was already heavily sagging by 55mm due to this constant load. Despite having this visual and mathematical proof, they blindly installed light, under-rated front springs (0–80kg) and standard rear springs (0–300kg) that immediately collapsed under the vehicle's actual weight. They then forced the wheel alignment to standard factory passenger-car specifications—reducing my front caster from over 3 degrees down to ~2 degrees. This toxic combination dropped the ride height below roadworthy limits and physically shoved the front wheels forward into the arches, causing the tyres to severely smash into the bodywork.2. Ruined Dash Electronics & Crushed WiringWhile routing their wiring looms for the driving lights and winches, their technicians pulled my dashboard apart and failed to reassemble it correctly. one_star_reviews.text:
I had two appointments booked with Dr James Lim—one for myself at 10:00 am and one for my partner at 10:30 am. I was running approximately 10 minutes late and, as a courtesy, contacted reception to advise them. I was told my 10:00 am appointment could no longer be accommodated, which I understood and accepted. To avoid delaying the doctor or inconveniencing other patients, I cancelled my appointment and, as advised by reception/Dr Lim, used my partner’s 10:30 am appointment instead.
My consultation was brief and finished at approximately 10:30 am. Despite this, my partner was then unable to attend their scheduled 10:30 am appointment and had to seek medical care elsewhere.

I fully understand the importance of punctuality and respecting a doctor’s time. Had my lateness caused the doctor to run behind, I would have accepted the situation without complaint. However, that was not the case. My partner had an appointment scheduled for 10:30 am, and I had finished by that time. Refusing to see my partner under these circumstances was extremely difficult to understand and felt unnecessarily punitive.

As a healthcare professional myself, I understand the importance of practice policies, patient flow and respecting clinicians’ time. However, policies should also be applied with reasonable judgement, clear communication and common sense. Unfortunately, I found the handling of this situation unnecessarily rigid, disappointing and lacking in these basic considerations.

I found Dr Lim to be a good physician and have no criticism of his clinical care. My concern is specifically with the management of the appointments and the handling of the situation by reception/administration.

I also note that a number of other reviews raise concerns regarding the reception and management team. Based on my own experience, I can understand why these concerns continue to be raised. My interaction with reception was unnecessarily abrupt and dismissive, which further contributed to an already disappointing experience.

I hope this constructive feedback is taken on board and translates into meaningful changes, particularly given the recurring concerns raised by other patients. Repeated feedback of this nature warrants genuine reflection and action. Patients should be able to expect professionalism, courtesy, accountability and sound judgement from every member of a healthcare practice—not only from its clinicians.

one_star_reviews.text:
This has been one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I have had with Officeworks\. I am extremely disappointed with the way the **Ravenhall store manager, Chris**, dealt with me\.

I came to Ravenhall with a large amount of construction drawings that I urgently needed printed\. Instead of trying to help me find a solution, I was repeatedly told what they **couldn’t do**\.

Chris told me they could only print one file of around 50 pages for approximately **$385**\. I paid the money upfront after being told I could collect it the next morning at around 8:00 am\. When I asked about additional sets, I was told I could be waiting **several weeks**\.

This is even more disappointing because approximately three weeks earlier I visited the same store with the same drawings and requested multiple laminated sets\. I was quoted around **$5,000** and told I would need to wait approximately a week because they were short\-staffed and someone was on leave\.

I then contacted **Officeworks Melton** with the SAME drawings and requested multiple sets\. Their staff were helpful, professional and solution\-focused\. They advised that my full printing order could be ready for collection the **NEXT DAY**\.

So how can one Officeworks store organise a large urgent printing job by the next day while Ravenhall repeatedly tells a customer that the work will take weeks?

When I returned to Ravenhall and showed them the paperwork and explained that Melton could complete the same work much faster, I expected the manager to listen and professionally address my concern\.

Instead, I felt I was met with **excuses, arguments and rude behaviour**\.

When I requested a refund of the approximately **$385 I had already paid**, my request was also refused\. The situation became unnecessarily argumentative when all I wanted was a reasonable explanation and professional customer service\.

My biggest complaint is about the **attitude and customer service from the manager, Chris**\. A manager should be setting an example for staff, listening to customers and trying to resolve problems—not making an already frustrated customer feel even worse\.

I work in construction and sometimes drawings are urgently required to keep work moving\. When a customer is prepared to spend hundreds or even thousands of dollars on printing, they should at least be treated respectfully\.

The difference between **Ravenhall and Melton was unbelievable**\. Melton tried to find a solution\. Ravenhall gave me excuses\.

Based on my experience, I would **NOT recommend Officeworks Ravenhall for urgent or large professional printing jobs**\.

Quite disappointed by the service offered by one of the team members at the Print + Create counter today.

I was looking to print some marketing materials off for my job which was an A4 document edge-to-edge, double sided document with the same paper and finish I had printed at the exact counter a few weeks ago without any troubles. However, I was told by the team member that they didn't have the options I was after, and that my specific request had to be placed as an order and couldn't be done the same day. I tried to explain to the team member that I previously had the same file printed at the counter without any issues and tried to explain the exact requirements I was after - because I finally had the opportunity to explain exactly what I wanted instead of the team member throwing incorrect options at me and making me feel rushed, she finally understood and went "Oh, you're just wanting a flyer done".

I felt like I was being rushed through the conversation. I had a similar experience when asking about quantities and pricing, where I didn’t feel I was given much opportunity to properly understand the different options.

When I presented my print file, I was then advised that the sizing/specifications were too large and could not be printed. I explained that on my previous visit, another team member resized the file for me without any mention of it being not allowed. This request was denied by the team member that helped me today as it was against policy. I was then advised to go back home to resize it myself before I could come back and get my print job done without any other acknowledgement - I truly felt rushed during this whole interaction with the team member and felt like she was trying to close up this interaction as quick as possible to attend the rest of the line of customers.

I completely understand that the Print + Create counter can get busy, lines can become long and team members can be under pressure. However, I would have appreciated the team member taking the time to focus on the customer in front of them.

Having had this negative experience today, I am grateful for the other team member who helped me out a few weeks ago in getting my files resized and printed smoothly even though it might have been against store policy.

Disappointing experience with an orthotist named LUKE Orsa.

After breaking my limb, I was referred by the hospital for a brace fitting. Unfortunately, my appointment started approximately 45 minutes late, and no apology or explanation was offered by Luke for the delay. Seriously?

What concerned me most was the LACK of empathy and communication throughout the consultation. As someone recovering from a significant injury, I expected a more supportive and patient-centred approach. Instead, the interaction felt extremely rushed, and I was left feeling like I was being moved through the appointment as quickly as possible.

The brace was fitted with very minimal explanation, and I was given little opportunity to ask questions or discuss my concerns. Considering I was charged over $80 for the appointment, I expected a higher level of care and professional service.

I was also disheartened to discover that the brace provided appeared to be a basic off-the-shelf product. I was charged over $250 for the brace, yet I later found what appeared to be the same or a very similar product available online for around $80. While I understand that healthcare providers may charge for fitting, assessment, and professional services, the overall value provided during the consultation did not justify the cost in my view.

Professionalism, communication, and empathy are especially important when dealing with vulnerable patients recovering from injuries. Unfortunately, this experience did not meet those expectations.

I hope this feedback encourages improvements in patient care and communication.

one_star_reviews.text:
We purchased our car from this dealership less than a year ago, and unfortunately, our experience has been extremely disappointing.
Approximately seven weeks after purchase, the vehicle suffered a major engine failure. When we contacted the dealership to advise them of what had happened, the response we received was extremely rude and left us very disappointed from the outset.

The dealership eventually agreed to have the vehicle towed back to them. Unfortunately, the car was left sitting on the side of the road overnight, with no communication regarding when it would be collected. We ultimately had to contact the RACQ service centre ourselves to find out whether the vehicle had been collected.
Once the dealership received the car, we were advised that the engine would be replaced with another engine that had significantly fewer kilometres. We were told this would be covered by the dealership. The repair took approximately eight weeks, with very little communication throughout the process.

I was eventually contacted and told the vehicle was ready to collect. When I picked it up, I asked specifically about the replacement engine. There appeared to be some confusion, so I asked, “It was replaced?” and was told, “Oh yeah, it was. We covered the cost for that.”
I then requested paperwork confirming the engine replacement and the work that had been carried out. I was told this would be arranged and forwarded to me.
When I later checked the VIN, however, it appeared to be the same original engine, despite us having been told that it had been replaced.

To be completely honest, I was simply relieved that the car was working again. There was no need for what felt like unnecessary confusion or misinformation about what work had actually been carried out. We simply wanted the vehicle repaired and to have accurate information about the repairs.
I last requested documentation regarding the engine work in February. It is now September, and I am still waiting.

Most recently the gearbox now needs to be replaced.

This has not been our only experience with vehicles purchased from this dealership.
At the same time, we also purchased a second vehicle from the dealership, meaning we spent more than $35,000 with them.

Unfortunately, we have experienced multiple problems with this vehicle as well, including:
• Wiring issues throughout the vehicle
• Dash lights not working when we received the vehicle — these were eventually repaired at the dealership's expense
• Water entering the vehicle when it rains, resulting in the footwell filling with water
• A ticking noise coming from the engine
• The air conditioner stopped working soon after we received the vehicle, despite being told it had been fixed
• The speedometer has also stopped working

After spending over $35,000 on two vehicles that were sold to us as roadworthy and described to us as “brilliant cars,” we certainly did not expect to be facing ongoing mechanical and electrical problems and having to spend additional money getting vehicles into a reliable condition.

The biggest disappointment for us has not simply been the number of problems we have encountered, but the lack of communication, transparency and confidence in the information provided to us throughout the process.

Based on our experience, my recommendation would be to purchase at your own risk and have your own independent mechanical inspection completed before committing to a purchase.
If you do purchase a vehicle from this dealership and subsequently experience problems, I would strongly recommend keeping detailed records of all communication and requesting documentation for any repairs or work carried out.

Unfortunately, based on our experience with both vehicles, we cannot recommend this dealership

1 STAR — EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING SERVICE

We took our lawn mower to General Mowers at the beginning of December for a service, with a suspected carburettor issue. We heard nothing for two months. When we finally called in early February to check on progress, we were told it was ready — despite receiving no prior notification.
The amount quoted at pickup was several dollars higher than what we'd been told when we dropped it off. When we explained we were dealing with financial hardship and needed a little time to arrange payment, the response from staff was unprofessional: we received an aggressive phone call and a text message in capital letters demanding we collect the mower immediately, despite having only just been informed it was ready after two months of silence.
We paid approximately $670 for the service. When we collected the mower, it wouldn't even start — staff had to jump-start it just to load it onto the trailer, and we had to trickle-charge it again at home. My husband used it for about an hour before it failed completely, with a visible hole in the motor. When we called to report this, we were told to bring it back in so they could "determine if it was broken," despite the damage being obvious. Given our financial situation and concern about being charged again, we didn't feel able to return it.
Overall, the communication was poor, the pricing changed without clear explanation, and the mower was returned to us in a non-functional state after two months and a significant cost.
One more thing for anyone reading reviews before choosing this business: we've noticed this company has a pattern of responding to other 1-star reviews by placing the blame entirely on the customer rather than addressing the concerns raised. We're not sharing this to be unkind — just so you go in with realistic expectations of how complaints are likely to be handled if something goes wrong.
We won't be using them again, and can't recommend them based on our experience.

When I explained I had existing appointments on Tuesday, the exchange became confusing and unhelpful, with the receptionist asking if I wanted to cancel an appointment I hadn't even booked.
As a person with a disability, I found the complete lack of basic accessibility, accommodation, and basic empathy deeply upsetting. Dismissing a patient in pain and struggling to hear is completely unprofessional. I strongly discourage anyone from using this practice—they were rude, dismissive, and showed a complete disregard for patient care.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would never use this funeral service again.

In 2018, I organised the funeral of my nephew, whom I had raised throughout much of his life. While his parents dealt with some arrangements through the funeral home, I was responsible for many of the personal and meaningful aspects of the service, including the photographs, obituary, coffin choice, coffin signage, memorial displays, ceremony arrangements, and keepsakes for family and friends. I undertook these responsibilities because I knew him better than anyone and was committed to ensuring the service reflected the life he lived.

On the day of the funeral, I arrived at the cathedral to ensure everything had been set up as arranged. While checking that the guest book was open, pens were available, and memorial items had been positioned correctly, I was approached by an older staff member with blonde hair, wearing a white hat. Without introducing herself, asking who I was, or making any attempt to understand my connection to the deceased, she abruptly stated, "Excuse me, leave that alone. That is how the family has asked for it to be." I consider this behaviour completely unacceptable.

Funeral professionals are entrusted to support grieving families during one of the most difficult days of their lives. Making assumptions about a person's role, particularly at a funeral, demonstrates a remarkable lack of judgement, professionalism, and sensitivity. At no point did this staff member attempt to ascertain who I was before speaking to me in a dismissive and confrontational manner.

I very quickly and politely corrected her. I informed her that not only was I his aunt, but that I had effectively been his primary parent and had personally organised much of the funeral. Only then did she retreat from the conversation.

The issue is not that she did not know who I was. The issue is that she felt comfortable approaching a grieving individual in such a rude and presumptuous manner without first seeking any context. In a profession centred around compassion and care, that standard of behaviour is entirely inappropriate.

Several family members and friends witnessed the interaction and were equally appalled by the way I was treated. They intervened immediately, recognising how distressing and disrespectful the situation was.

Nearly a decade later, this incident still remains a defining memory I have of my nephew’s funeral service. Instead of feeling supported during an incredibly painful loss by the funeral directors, I was forced to defend my place in my nephew's life and my role in arranging his farewell. That should never happen to any grieving family member.

Respect, empathy, and professionalism are the minimum standards families should expect. Unfortunately, those standards were not met on the day of my nephew's funeral.

This was disappointing, as I had hoped it would be delivered earlier. I also found her tone somewhat abrupt, but I let it go.

I then asked whether it would be possible to receive a photo of the arrangement before delivery. When I saw what had been sent, I was extremely disappointed. The arrangement looked nothing like what I expected based on the website, and certainly did not reflect the price paid.

I phoned Kobe to express my concerns about the arrangement and the quality of the flowers. The arrangement received consisted of one sunflower, one tiger lily, a few foliage leaves, and what appeared to be mostly inexpensive daisies. have been unable to work and significantly disabled since Saturday afternoon following a massage at your premises at approximately 2:30 pm with Bepe.

During the massage, I repeatedly experienced significant pain and told the therapist that the stretching and manipulation were hurting me.

Despite my complaints, she continued with forceful manipulation around my neck, shoulder, underarm and arm. At times, the treatment felt less like a massage and more like I was in a boxing ring.

Of particular concern, the therapist repeatedly pressed and manipulated areas around the nerves in my arm and underarm. She appeared to be trying to locate my ulnar nerve, repeatedly pressing and pinching the area. Even when I moved my arm away because of the pain, she returned to the same area and continued.

Since that massage, I have been diagnosed with cervical radiculopathy and am experiencing severe neurological pain radiating from my neck down my right arm, together with significant loss of control and function of my right arm. I am in constant pain and now need to be assessed by a neurosurgeon.

This is not simply a complaint about an unpleasant or overly firm massage. I have sustained a diagnosed injury with significant neurological symptoms, loss of function, ongoing pain, medical expenses and inability to work.

I am extremely concerned about the therapist's apparent lack of understanding of basic anatomy and, particularly, the risks associated with forceful manipulation around the neck and major nerves.

Most concerning was that she continued despite me communicating that what she was doing was painful.
I cannot recommend this business and would urge others to exercise extreme care.

I am asking management to urgently investigate this incident and take appropriate action regarding the therapist involved. Please ensure that your staff understand anatomy, the limits of what they should be manipulating.

All you need to do is read the reviews and see the pattern, this is a civil issue..

My experience with The Victoria Clinic and the complaints process that followed has been deeply disappointing.

Following my experience as a patient, I raised concerns through The Victoria Clinic and Healthscope’s internal complaints processes. When I was dissatisfied with the way my concerns were addressed, I continued pursuing the matter through external avenues, including AHPRA and the Health Complaints Commissioner (HCC).

This has been an extraordinarily lengthy and difficult process. I have had to repeatedly follow up, request documentation and records, correspond with multiple organisations, and continue advocating for myself when I felt my concerns had not been adequately recognised or examined.

After almost a year of persistence, my concerns are now receiving further attention and investigation. I am grateful that the matter is finally progressing, but I believe no patient should have to work this hard simply to have serious concerns about their healthcare properly heard and considered.

I am deliberately limiting this review to my personal experience and will not publicly discuss matters that remain under investigation. My purpose in writing this is not to prejudge the outcome, but to encourage other patients to understand their rights.

If you believe something has gone wrong with your treatment or care, document what happened, obtain copies of your medical records, communicate your concerns in writing, retain your correspondence, and seek independent advice about the appropriate complaints process.

Patients should not be afraid to ask questions or respectfully challenge decisions concerning their own healthcare. Accountability, transparency and a willingness to listen to patients are essential parts of a trustworthy health system.

My experience has taught me one thing above all: persistence matters. If you genuinely believe your rights as a patient have not been respected, do not assume that an initial rejection or unsatisfactory response must be the end of the matter. Use the appropriate channels, remain factual, preserve your evidence and continue advocating for yourself.

Every patient deserves to be heard, treated with dignity, and given a fair opportunity to seek answers and accountability.
